answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each new identity to lock a scarce token before it can trade. Honest activity gradually earns release of the stake and access to larger orders; proven fraud burns it. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake vertex separately, and cannot cheaply copy one trusted agent’s history. Even on an island of disconnected newcomers, the attacker pays upfront for each identity and risks losing the stake on every fraudulent voyage.
